title: GoHighLevel Pricing 2026: When $297 Becomes $2,267
desc: Seven GoHighLevel add-ons bill per sub-account, so the flat $297 plan is 13 percent of a ten client bill. Full 2026 plan, usage and add-on math, verified Aug 13.
keywords: gohighlevel pricing, gohighlevel pricing 2026, gohighlevel plans, how much does gohighlevel cost, gohighlevel hidden costs, gohighlevel add-on pricing, gohighlevel per sub-account cost, gohighlevel ai pricing, gohighlevel ai employee pricing, gohighlevel voice ai cost, gohighlevel $97 vs $297
cta: Want a GoHighLevel build that pays for itself?
body:
Quick answer: GoHighLevel has three self-serve plans in 2026: Starter at $97 per month, Unlimited at $297, and Agency Pro at $497, plus a quote-based Enterprise tier. Those three numbers have not moved all year. What decides your actual bill is the layer underneath them, because seven of the fourteen add-ons HighLevel lists are priced per sub-account, not per agency. Turn the full client stack on for ten clients and you move $1,970 a month in add-ons against a $297 platform fee, so the plan you shopped for is 13 percent of the invoice. That is not a hidden fee and it is not a scandal: almost all of it is resellable. It is only a cost if you forgot to price it into the retainer.

Below is the full 2026 picture: plans, usage rates, the AI layer, and the add-on menu, with the arithmetic done rather than described. Every number was re-verified on August 13, 2026 against HighLevel's own pricing page, its Pricing Guide (last modified June 18, 2026) and its AI Product Pricing doc (last modified July 31, 2026). For features rather than invoices, read our honest GoHighLevel review, and for the head-to-head against the other agency all-in-one, see GoHighLevel vs Keap.

GoHighLevel pricing at a glance

  • Starter, $97 per month or $970 per year: the full platform, unlimited contacts and unlimited users, capped at 3 sub-accounts. No API access, no rebilling.
  • Unlimited, $297 per month or $2,970 per year: adds unlimited sub-accounts, basic API access, white-labelled desktop app, and rebilling of phone and email usage to clients at cost.
  • Agency Pro, $497 per month or $4,970 per year: adds SaaS Mode, automated sub-account creation, rebilling with your own markup, user and agent reporting, and advanced API access.
  • Enterprise, quote only: the fourth tier most guides skip. Bundles a dedicated CSM, custom development, premium support, higher API limits, and the white-label mobile app and HIPAA compliance included rather than billed as add-ons.
  • Annual billing: exactly ten months for twelve, about 17 percent off. That is roughly $81 per month on Starter, $248 on Unlimited, $414 on Agency Pro.
  • Free trial: 14 days on every plan, card required. Usage-based telecom fees can still be charged during it. Month to month, no contract, cancel from the dashboard.

The subscription line will not surprise you. The surprises live in the add-on menu, the usage wallet and the AI plans, so that is where most of this page goes.

The add-ons that bill per client, not per agency

The reason to pay $297 instead of $97 is unlimited sub-accounts: your software cost stops scaling with your client count. That is true of the plan. It is not true of the menu attached to it. Of the fourteen add-ons on HighLevel's pricing page, seven carry the words "per sub-account", and because the two AI plans are alternatives rather than additions, six of them can run on the same client at once.

Per client, per month, at HighLevel's published rates:

  • SEO powered by Search Atlas, $79
  • Branded Client Portal App, $49
  • Online Listings, $30
  • Premium Prospecting Tool, $29
  • WhatsApp integration, $10 plus per-conversation usage
  • AI Employee, $50 on the Growth plan or $97 on Unlimited

The five non-AI items total $197 per client per month. Add AI Employee Unlimited and it is $294. Now do the multiplication HighLevel does not do for you:

  • One client with everything switched on costs $294, which is $3 less than the entire Unlimited plan.
  • At two clients the non-AI stack alone ($394) already exceeds the $297 plan.
  • At ten clients you are moving $2,267 a month ($297 plus ten times $197), of which the plan is 13 percent. Swap in AI Employee Unlimited and it is $3,237, and the plan is 9 percent.

Then there is the flat, agency-level menu, which does not scale with clients but is heavy on its own: dedicated email IP $59 per IP, HighLevel Certification $97, HIPAA compliance $297, premium support $500, white-label mobile app $497. That is $1,450 a month, or 2.9 times the entire Agency Pro plan and about 15 times Starter. Two lines deserve to be read twice, and neither flatters the product we are an affiliate for: premium support at $500 costs $3 more than the whole $497 Agency Pro plan, and HIPAA compliance at $297 costs exactly as much as the Unlimited plan, doubling that bill, and HighLevel states it cannot be deactivated once enabled. The billing guide adds two more the pricing page omits: Whitelabel Zap at $50 per month and a one-off Advanced Account Setup at $1,000.

The honest part, and it matters: almost every per-client add-on is resellable. HighLevel charges your agency for each sub-account the feature is enabled on, and you can switch reselling on and recover the cost, at cost on the $297 plan or with your own markup on the $497 plan. So $2,267 is not a loss. It is cash flowing through your account. It becomes a loss the moment somebody enables SEO or Listings for a client "to try it" and nobody turns reselling on. If you run more than a handful of sub-accounts, audit the reselling toggles before you audit anything else. This is the single most common way agencies quietly subsidise their own clients, and it is exactly the kind of thing we fix on GoHighLevel builds.

What changed in HighLevel pricing since July

Pricing guides rot quietly, so here is what actually moved since our July 15 update. The three plan prices and the entire usage rate card are unchanged and re-verified.

  • The Summer of AI promotion ends September 1, 2026. Ask AI and AI Studio are free until then and billed at token cost afterwards. If you have built anything on Ask AI this summer, its price tag arrives in about three weeks. This is the most actionable date on the page.
  • Workflow Pro is now four tiers, not three, and the overage rate now falls as you climb: Free at $0, Starter $10, Growth $25, Scale $50, with overages at $0.01, $0.008, $0.006 and $0.004 per execution. The free tier is 100 executions for the lifetime of the account, not per month.
  • The add-on menu is now consolidated on the public pricing page. Until recently you had to read the billing guide to find these numbers. That is a real transparency improvement and worth crediting.
  • Still true from our earlier corrections: Voice AI was unbundled on May 20, 2026, so the roughly $0.163 per minute blended figure we published in June is historical and should not be used for budgeting; and AI Employee Unlimited does cover outbound Voice AI and the widget, not inbound only.
  • Unchanged and still the most-missed exclusion: Agent Studio is in no plan at any price and stays pay per use, including on the $97 Unlimited AI plan.

Starter at $97: right for one business, tight for an agency

Starter is the whole product, not a crippled version: CRM, funnels, automations, calendars, reputation management, courses, unlimited contacts and unlimited users. The single wall is 3 sub-accounts, meaning your agency account plus two clients. There is no API access and no rebilling, so any SMS, email or AI your clients burn comes out of your wallet and stays there. Note what that does to the add-on maths above: on Starter every per-client add-on is a pure cost with no recovery mechanism.

Right for a single business, a consultant with one or two retainers, or anyone learning the platform before betting an agency on it.

Unlimited at $297: the agency default

For $200 more you get unlimited sub-accounts, which is the whole point: add your fortieth client and the plan line is still $297. You also get basic API access, white-label branding on the desktop app, and rebilling at cost. Turn rebilling on the day you upgrade. Bill two clients $300 or more and the plan has paid for itself. We show the full break-even maths in is GoHighLevel worth it.

Agency Pro at $497: SaaS Mode and markup money

Agency Pro exists to let you sell GoHighLevel as your own software: publish your own plans, take Stripe payments, and have client accounts provision themselves. The number that pays for it is rebilling with markup. On Unlimited you pass usage through at cost; on Agency Pro you set the client price above cost and keep the difference. AI Employee rebilling in particular requires this plan. Ten SaaS customers at $197 is $1,970 recurring against a $497 bill. Full setup in our SaaS Mode guide.

Do not buy it for features. Buy it when you have an offer ready to launch.

The usage costs nobody puts on the pricing page

Phone and email run through a prepaid Agency Wallet that auto-recharges your card. Unit prices are small, volumes are not. Per HighLevel's billing guide:

  • Email: $0.675 per 1,000 sends on every plan. A 100,000-send month is $67.50.
  • SMS and calls: billed at Twilio parity, so roughly $0.0079 per segment and $0.014 per minute outbound in the US, plus a couple of dollars per number per month. Long texts split into segments, so a 300-character blast counts two or three times.
  • No more Stripe markup: HighLevel removed the 5 percent uplift it used to add to phone charges. Since October 1, 2025 phone usage bills at exact carrier passthrough.
  • Email validation: $2.50 per 1,000 checks. Worth it to protect deliverability.
  • Premium workflow actions: $0.01 per execution, covering Decision Maker, Intent Detection, Summarize Text and Translate.

Workflow Pro is the one add-on where the arithmetic clearly favours you, which is worth saying plainly because on this page most of the arithmetic goes the other way. Ten dollars buys 10,000 executions that would cost $100 at the pay-as-you-go rate, so the Starter tier is ten times cheaper per execution and pays for itself above 1,000 executions a month. Working the overage rates through: Growth at $25 beats Starter above 11,875 executions a month, and Scale at $50 beats Growth above 34,167. Almost nobody on the free tier should stay there, because its 100 executions are a lifetime allowance.

Two more usage traps worth pricing before you sell them. WordPress hosting has a cliff: the Utility plan is $220 for 25 sites, or $8.80 a site, and the next step up is Truly Unlimited at $497. Host 26 sites and your per-site cost more than doubles to $19.12, and Utility stays the cheaper option per site until you pass about 56 sites. And Agent Studio can get expensive fast: it sits outside every AI plan, and video generation runs $0.15 per second of video on Veo3 Fast or $0.40 on Veo3. That is $9 and $24 per finished minute, on a $97 plan that calls itself unlimited.

AI pricing in 2026: three modes, not two

The AI suite is priced separately from the plans, and there are three billing modes, each set per enabled sub-account.

  • 1. Pay per use. No monthly fee. Conversation AI bills tokens at model rates, for example GPT-5 at $1.25 per million input and $10 per million output, or GPT-5 Mini at $0.25 and $2.00. Reviews AI is $0.01 per review, Content AI $0.063 per image and $0.0945 per 1,000 words.
  • 2. AI Employee Growth, $50 per month. Includes 1,000 Conversation AI responses, 100 Voice AI minutes covering inbound, outbound and widget combined, unlimited Reviews and Content AI, and included Ask AI and AI Studio usage. Go over and the excess bills at pay-per-use rates automatically; access is not cut off.
  • 3. AI Employee Unlimited, $97 per month. Unlimited Conversation AI, Voice AI across all three modes, Reviews AI and Content AI, subject to fair use. Ask AI and AI Studio get 3x the Growth allowance rather than true unlimited, measured in 5-hour windows.

Voice AI is the number to watch, because since May 20, 2026 it is a stack rather than a rate: Voice Engine at $0.045 per minute, plus text to speech, plus model tokens, plus the phone call itself. The two choices you make inside that stack swing the bill more than the plan does. On text to speech, OpenAI and Cartesia are $0.015 per minute and ElevenLabs V3 is $0.170, an 11x spread. On the model, Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite is $0.075 per million tokens and Claude 4.5 Sonnet is $3.00, a 40x spread. HighLevel's own worked example puts a 10-minute call on OpenAI TTS at $0.60 in voice cost before tokens and phone charges. Pick ElevenLabs V3 and Claude for the same call and you are in a different price class entirely.

One structural note: on pay per use and on Growth, AI cost is a function of conversation length, not of conversation value. Budget it like telecom, not like software. If you want the calls handled properly rather than metered badly, that is what our AI automation team builds.

Where annual billing saves nothing

The three plans are consistent: pay annually and you get ten months for twelve, a clean 16.7 percent off. The add-ons are not consistent, and two of them are worth checking before you commit.

  • White-label mobile app: $497 per month or $1,491 per quarter. That is exactly three times $497. The quarterly option is not a discount, it is the same price with a longer commitment.
  • Online Listings: $30 per month, $150 for six months, or $300 per year. The six-month and the annual plan both work out at $25 per month, so committing for a year buys no extra discount over committing for six. Take the shorter one.
  • Premium support and certification do follow the ten-for-twelve rule: $500 per month or $5,000 per year, $97 per month or $970 per year.
  • WordPress hosting uses three different annual discounts: about 10 percent on Standard ($108 a year), 5.5 percent on Utility ($2,496), and the full 16.7 percent on Truly Unlimited ($4,968).

What HighLevel actually gives you free

A pricing page that only counts costs is a bad pricing page, so here is the other side, all of it verified on the same documents. Ad Manager is now $0 per month for agencies with no platform fee, and you can still resell it at any price you like; client ad spend is separate. Funnel and Website AI is free on every plan, including pay per use, at 1,000 prompts per day per sub-account. Workflow AI Builder and Generate with AI are free with daily limits that reset within 24 hours. Unlimited users on every plan, including the $97 one, is the genuinely unusual thing here: most agency CRMs charge per seat, which is the core of our GoHighLevel vs Keap comparison.

Three realistic monthly bills

  • Solo operator, one business, Starter. $97 plan plus roughly $10 to $30 of email and SMS. Call it $110 to $130 a month, all in, with no add-ons enabled.
  • Ten-client agency, Unlimited, lean. $297 plan plus $70 to $150 of usage across ten sub-accounts, most of it rebillable at cost. Real net cost stays close to $297 if rebilling is on from day one.
  • Ten-client agency, Unlimited, full client stack. $2,267 a month, or $3,237 with AI Employee Unlimited on every client. Nearly all of it is recoverable through reselling. The margin question is not whether you spend it, it is whether your retainer prices it.

How to pay less

  • Turn rebilling on the day you upgrade to $297. It is the single largest recoverable line on the whole bill and it is a toggle.
  • Audit your reselling toggles per sub-account, not per agency. Anything enabled for a client and not resold is pure margin loss, and it repeats monthly.
  • Pick AI Employee Growth over Unlimited until you measure. At $50 versus $97 per sub-account, across ten clients that is $470 a month, and overages bill automatically rather than cutting you off.
  • Choose OpenAI or Cartesia for text to speech unless a client is paying for the premium voice. The 11x spread is the largest single lever in Voice AI.
  • Buy a Workflow Pro tier the moment you clear 1,000 premium executions a month.
  • Do not enable HIPAA to win one deal. $297 a month forever, and HighLevel says it cannot be switched off.

Which plan should you pick in 2026?

Starter at $97 if you run one business or two retainers and want to learn the platform. Unlimited at $297 the moment you have a third client, because that is where the sub-account cap bites and where rebilling starts paying for the upgrade by itself. Agency Pro at $497 only when you have a productised offer to launch, because SaaS Mode and markup rebilling are the only things you are buying and they are worthless without an offer behind them.

The plan choice is the easy part, and it is the part every other pricing guide stops at. The decision that actually moves your margin is which per-client add-ons you enable and whether every one of them is resold. Get that wrong across ten sub-accounts and the plan you agonised over is 13 percent of what you pay. If you would rather not audit that yourself, we do it as part of every build: hire a GoHighLevel developer.

faqs: How much does GoHighLevel cost per month in 2026?

GoHighLevel has three self-serve plans: Starter at $97 per month, Unlimited at $297 and Agency Pro at $497, with a quote-based Enterprise tier above them. Annual billing is ten months for twelve, so about $81, $248 and $414 per month. Usage for email, SMS, calls and AI is billed on top through a prepaid Agency Wallet, and optional add-ons are billed separately. All prices verified on HighLevel's pricing page on August 13, 2026.
Which GoHighLevel add-ons are charged per client?

Seven of the fourteen add-ons on HighLevel's pricing page are priced per sub-account: AI Employee Growth at $50, AI Employee Unlimited at $97, Branded Client Portal App at $49, Online Listings at $30, Premium Prospecting at $29, SEO by Search Atlas at $79 and WhatsApp at $10. Because the two AI plans are alternatives, the maximum simultaneous stack on one client is $294 per month. The rest, including HIPAA at $297, premium support at $500 and the white-label mobile app at $497, are flat agency-level charges.
Does the $297 Unlimited plan really stop your costs scaling?

The plan line stops scaling, the add-on line does not. Unlimited gives you unlimited sub-accounts for a flat $297, so adding your fortieth client does not change the subscription. But the seven per-sub-account add-ons scale exactly with client count, so ten clients on the full non-AI stack adds $1,970 a month. The important detail is that those add-ons are resellable, at cost on the $297 plan and with markup on the $497 plan, so they are only a real cost if reselling is left switched off.
What are the hidden costs of GoHighLevel?

Nothing is technically hidden, but four things are easy to miss. Usage runs through an auto-recharging Agency Wallet, so email at $0.675 per 1,000 sends and SMS at Twilio parity rates never appear on the pricing page. Agent Studio is excluded from every AI plan and stays pay per use, with Veo3 video at $0.40 per second. HIPAA compliance at $297 per month cannot be deactivated once enabled. And WordPress hosting jumps from $220 for 25 sites to $497 the moment you host a 26th.
Is GoHighLevel annual billing worth it?

On the plans, yes: annual is exactly ten months for twelve, a 16.7 percent discount on all three tiers. On the add-ons it varies and two are worth avoiding. The white-label mobile app is $497 per month or $1,491 per quarter, which is precisely three times the monthly price and therefore no discount at all. Online Listings costs $25 per month effective on both the six-month and the annual plan, so the longer commitment buys nothing. Premium support and the certification program do follow the ten-for-twelve rule.
When does the GoHighLevel Summer of AI promotion end?

September 1, 2026. Ask AI and AI Studio are free under the promotion until then, and both revert to token-cost billing afterwards. If you have built client workflows on Ask AI over the summer, budget for those charges arriving in September. Agent Studio was never part of the promotion and has always been pay per use across all three AI billing modes.
